Basketball Stats, Height, Age |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/236057-malachi-emmanuel-flynn |website=FIBA Basketball |access-date=9 October 2025}} (born May 9, 1998) ({{IPAc-en|audio=En-us-Malachi.ogg|ˈ|m|æ|l|ə|k|aɪ|}}) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Bahçeşehir Koleji S.K.|Bahçeşehir Koleji]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL). He represents [[Turkey men's national basketball team|Turkey]] internationally. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State Cougars]] and the [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State Aztecs]]. He was selected 29th by the [[Toronto Raptors]] in the first round of the [[2020 NBA draft]]. ==High school career== Flynn is the youngest of seven children. He stood 5'2 during his freshman season in high school, then grew to 5'6 as a sophomore before a growth spurt took him to his current height of 6'1.{{cite news |last1=Bennett |first1=Brian |title=Malachi Flynn is the transfer who is leading surprising San Diego State |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1475593/2019/12/20/malachi-flynn-is-the-transfer-that-is-leading-surprising-san-diego-state/ |access-date=January 2, 2020 |work=[[The Athletic]] |date=December 20, 2019}} As a senior at [[Bellarmine Preparatory School|Bellarmine Prep]], Flynn averaged 29.7 points, 6.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists per game, while shooting 48 percent from the floor. He earned a host of accolades, including [[The News Tribune]]'s All-Area player of the year, [[Associated Press]] Washington player of the year, the Class 4A player of the year by the Washington Interscholastic Basketball Coaches Association, and the 4A Narrows League MVP as a senior. His 743 points as a senior set the single-season mark at Bellarmine Prep, and he finished with 1,625 career points, second only to [[Abdul Gaddy]].{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Lauren |title=Former Bellarmine Prep, WSU standout announces transfer to San Diego State |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/high-school/article210642879.html |access-date=January 2, 2020 |work=[[The News Tribune]] |date=May 7, 2018}} Flynn originally committed to [[Pacific Tigers men's basketball|Pacific]] before reopening his recruitment late in the signing period.{{cite news |last1=Milles |first1=Todd |title=WSU's late find — Flynn — a basketball life saver |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/college/washington-state-university/article124018714.html |access-date=January 2, 2020 |work=[[The News Tribune]] |date=December 31, 2016}} He signed with the [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State Cougars]] on April 13, 2016.{{cite news |last1=Thorpe |first1=Jacob |title=Kent effusive about newest recruit Malachi Flynn |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2016/apr/13/kent-effusive-about-newest-recruit-malachi-flynn/ |access-date=January 2, 2020 |work=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |date=April 3, 2016}} ==College career== [[File:Malachi Flynn.jpg|thumb|right|Flynn with [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]] in 2018]] In November 2016, Flynn scored 27 points in an 83–76 victory over [[Utah Valley Wolverines men's basketball|Utah Valley]], which is sixth most for a Cougar freshman in history. As a freshman at Washington State, he averaged 9.7 points per game and shot 38.7 percent from three-point range. Flynn averaged 15.8 points and 4.3 assists per game while shooting 41.3 percent from the field as a sophomore. He was the top player on a team that finished 12–19. Following the season, Flynn announced he was transferring. After receiving interest from [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]], [[Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball|Texas A&M]], [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]] and [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]], Flynn signed with [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State]] in May 2018.{{cite news |last1=Zarrett |first1=E. Jay |title=Former Washington State guard Malachi Flynn transferring to San Diego State |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/former-washington-state-guard-malachi-flynn-transferring-san-diego-state-creighton-baylor-texas-am/6olkxpdhb3cb18t8j2ka0abhw |access-date=January 2, 2020 |work=[[Sporting News]] |date=May 7, 2018 |archive-date=January 2, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200102212820/https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/former-washington-state-guard-malachi-flynn-transferring-san-diego-state-creighton-baylor-texas-am/6olkxpdhb3cb18t8j2ka0abhw |url-status=dead }} Coming into his redshirt junior season, Flynn was named the preseason [[Mountain West Conference|Mountain West]] player of the year by Mountain West Wire.{{cite news |last1=Maciejewski |first1=Michael |title=The Case For Malachi Flynn As Mountain West's Best Player |url=https://mwwire.com/2019/10/16/the-case-for-malachi-flynn-as-mountain-wests-best-player/ |access-date=January 2, 2020 |work=Mountain West Wire |date=October 16, 2019}} In a game in which he otherwise shot poorly, Flynn hit a last-second three-point shot on December 8 to defeat [[San Jose State Spartans men's basketball|San Jose State]] 59–57.{{cite news |last1=Zeigler |first1=Mark |title=Aztecs survive against San Jose State on late 3 by Malachi Flynn |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/story/2019-12-08/aztecs-survive-against-san-jose-state-on-late-3-by-malachi-flynn |access-date=January 2, 2020 |work=[[San Diego Union Tribune]] |date=December 8, 2019}} He was named to the midseason watchlist for the [[Wooden Award]].{{cite news |title=Gonzaga's Filip Petrusev among new faces on Wooden Award midseason list |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28448986/gonzaga-filip-petrusev-new-faces-wooden-award-midseason-list |access-date=January 10, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=January 8, 2020}} On February 29, 2020, Flynn scored a career-high 36 points, the most by any Aztec since 2005, shooting 13-of-20 from the floor in an 83–76 comeback win over [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|Nevada]].{{cite news |title=No. 5 San Diego St. overcomes 2nd-half deficit, tops Nevada |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401173804 |access-date=March 1, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 29, 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Flynn was named [[Mountain West Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Mountain West Player of the Year]] and Defensive Player of the Year.{{cite press release|url=https://themw.com/news/2020/3/3/mountain-west-announces-2019-20-mens-basketball-all-conference-team.aspx |title=Mountain West Announces 2019-20 Men's Basketball All-Conference Team |publisher=Mountain West Conference |date=March 3, 2020 |access-date=March 3, 2020}} He averaged 17.6 points, 5.1 assists, and 4.5 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last1=Dauster |first1=Rob |title=NBC Sports College Basketball All-American Teams |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/03/10/college-basketball-all-american-teams/ |access-date=March 16, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=March 10, 2020}} Following the season, Flynn declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=San Diego State's Malachi Flynn entering NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29049281/san-diego-state-malachi-flynn-entering-nba-draft |access-date=April 17, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=April 17, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Toronto Raptors (2020–2023)=== Flynn was selected with the 29th pick in the first round of the [[2020 NBA draft]] by the [[Toronto Raptors]],{{cite news |last1=Smith |first1=Lauren |title=Tacoma's Malachi Flynn went from under-recruited high schooler to first-round NBA Draft pick |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/high-school/article247270869.html |access-date=November 18, 2020 |work=[[Tacoma News Tribune]] |date=November 18, 2020}} the first San Diego State player to be drafted in the first round since [[Kawhi Leonard]] in 2011. He made his debut for the Raptors on December 23, 2020, playing one minute against the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web|title=Pelicans beat relocated Raptors 113-99; Van Gundy wins debut|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401267174|access-date=February 2, 2021|work=[[ESPN]]|date=December 23, 2020}} On February 3, 2021, Flynn was assigned to the Raptors' [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Raptors 905]].{{cite web|title=Malachi Flynn: Toronto Raptors rookie guard assigned to Raptors 905 for G League bubble|url=https://ca.nba.com/news/malachi-flynn-toronto-raptors-rookie-guard-assigned-to-raptors-905-for-g-league-bubble/105fydry89srv1wcez2om6r3il|access-date=February 3, 2021|work=NBA.com|date=February 3, 2021}} On February 18, 2021, Flynn was recalled from his NBA G League assignment. On April 10, 2021, Flynn scored a then career-high 20 points and dished out a career-high 11 assists with two rebounds and steals in a 135–115 win against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite web|title=Trent scores career-high 44, Raptors rout Cavaliers 135-115|url=https://www.espn.co.uk/nba/recap?gameId=401307587|access-date=April 11, 2021|work=[[ESPN]]|date=April 10, 2021}} On April 14, 2021, Flynn scored a then career-high 22 points with five rebounds, three assists and two steals in a 103–108 loss against the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|title=Malachi Flynn took over late and nearly led Raptors to comeback win|url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2021/04/13/raptors-malachi-flynn-fourth-quarter-highlights/|access-date=April 16, 2021|work=USA Today|date=April 14, 2021}} On May 4, 2021, Flynn was named Eastern Conference Rookie of the Month for April 2021.{{Cite web|title=Raptors guard Malachi Flynn named East's Rookie of the Month for April|url=https://www.yahoo.com/now/nba-raptors-guard-malachi-flynn-wins-rookie-of-the-month-for-april-203744893.html|access-date=May 4, 2021|website=www.yahoo.com|date=May 4, 2021 |language=en-US}} On March 4, 2022, Flynn scored a season-high 20 points, alongside three rebounds and eight assists, in a 97–103 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]].{{Cite web |title=Magic End 9-Game Skid Against Raptors With 103-97 Victory |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100458 |access-date=February 1, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} ===New York Knicks (2023–2024)=== On December 30, 2023, Flynn, along with [[O.G. Anunoby]] and [[Precious Achiuwa]], were traded to the [[New York Knicks]] in exchange for [[RJ Barrett]], [[Immanuel Quickley]] and a second-round pick.{{cite web|title=New York Knicks Acquire OG Anunoby, Precious Achiuwa, and Malachi Flynn|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/new-york-knicks-acquire-og-anunoby-precious-achiuwa-and-malachi-flynn|website=NBA.com|date=December 30, 2023|access-date=December 30, 2023}} ===Detroit Pistons (2024)=== On February 8, 2024, Flynn, [[Ryan Arcidiacono]], [[Evan Fournier]], [[Quentin Grimes]] and two second-round picks were traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in exchange for [[Bojan Bogdanović]] and [[Alec Burks]].{{cite web|title=Detroit Pistons Acquire Quentin Grimes, Evan Fournier, Malachi Flynn, Ryan Arcidiacono, Two Future Second Round Draft Picks and Cash Considerations From New York|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-acquire-quentin-grimes-evan-fournier-malachi-flynn-ryan-arcidiacono-two-future-second-round-draft-picks-and-cash-considerations-from-new-york|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}} On April 3, Flynn scored a career-high 50 points against the [[Atlanta Hawks]], tying him with [[Nick Anderson (basketball)|Nick Anderson]] for the second-highest amount of points scored by a player coming off the bench in NBA history, behind [[Jamal Crawford]].{{cite web|title=Detroit Pistons vs Atlanta Hawks Apr 3, 2024 Box Scores|url=https://www.nba.com/game/det-vs-atl-0022301104/box-score|website=NBA.com}}{{cite web|title=Pistons guard Malachi Flynn becomes 3rd player to score 50 points off the bench|url=https://www.nba.com/news/pistons-malachi-flynn-scores-50-off-the-bench|website=NBA.com|date=April 3, 2024|access-date=April 4, 2024}}{{cite web|first=Victor R.|last=Lopez M.|title=5 NBA players with the most points scored off the bench in a single game|url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/basketball/5-nba-players-points-scored-bench-single-game|website=Sportskeeda.com|date=November 8, 2022|access-date=April 3, 2024}} Additionally, he became the player with the lowest career scoring average with 5.2 to score 50 points in an NBA game, a record previously set by [[Terrence Ross]], who averaged 7.4 points per game at the time.{{cite web |last=Maloney |first=Jack |date=April 4, 2024 |title=Pistons' Malachi Flynn records most surprising 50-point game in NBA history |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/pistons-malachi-flynn-makes-history-with-most-surprising-50-point-game-in-nba-history/ |access-date=September 1, 2024 |website=CBSSports.com}} ===Austin Spurs (2024–2025)=== On August 7, 2024, Flynn signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]],{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Spurs Sign Malachi Flynn To Exhibit 10 Contract|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/08/spurs-to-sign-malachi-flynn.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=August 8, 2024|access-date=September 1, 2024}}{{cite web|title=Report: Former Raptors guard Malachi Flynn signs one-year deal with Spurs|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/report-former-raptors-guard-malachi-flynn-signs-one-year-deal-with-spurs/|website=Sportsnet.ca|date=August 7, 2024|access-date=August 17, 2024}} but was waived on October 19.{{cite web|author=sasmcasey|title=Spurs Announce 2024-25 Opening Night Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-announce-2024-25-opening-night-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 19, 2024}} On October 29, he joined the [[Austin Spurs]].{{cite web|title=Austin Spurs Announce 2024 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/austin-spurs-announce-2024-training-camp-roster/n-6160743|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 29, 2024|access-date=November 3, 2024}} === Charlotte Hornets (2025) === On February 28, 2025, Flynn signed a 10-day contract with the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{Cite web |date=2025-03-01 |title=Charlotte Hornets sign Malachi Flynn - At The Hive |url=https://atthehive.com/2025/03/01/charlotte-hornets-sign-malachi-flynn/ |access-date=2025-03-01 |website=atthehive.com |language=en-US}} ===Bahçeşehir Koleji (2025–present)=== On June 1, 2025, Flynn signed with [[Bahçeşehir Koleji S.K.|Bahçeşehir Koleji]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite tweet |user=BKBasketbol |number=1933437743813853321 |title=Malachi Flynn, Bahçeşehir Koleji’nde!}} On November 5, Flynn received a Hoops Agents Player of the Week Award for Round 6. He had the game-high 36 points, 4 rebounds, and 5 assists for his team's victory.{{cite web |title=Malachi Flynn gets MVP of the Week award for Turkish BSL |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Turkey/news/966121/Malachi-Flynn-gets-MVP-of-the-Week-award-for-Turkish-BSL |website=www.eurobasket.com |access-date=5 November 2025}} In the regular season of the [[2025–26 EuroCup Basketball|2025-26 EuroCup]] Flynn led Bahçeşehir in points (17.8), assists (4.0), steals (1.7) per game and PIR (18.9). {{cite web |title=Bahcesehir College Istanbul Statistics |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/eurocup/teams/bahcesehir-college-istanbul/statistics/bah/?season=2025-26&phase=REGULAR%20SEASON&statistic=pointsScored&sortDirection=descending |website=www.euroleaguebasketball.net |access-date=16 February 2026}} On June 16, 2026, Flynn re–signed with the team on a one–year contract.{{Cite web|title=Malachi Flynn officially stays in
